prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.
Recommended for 'Grundlagen der Fügetechnik' course: Materials Science

learning_outcomes.text: Students can describe essential fundamentals and typical characteristics of the most important joining processes and establish important connections between the structure and properties of various materials.
Students can explain material science processes related to foundry technology, a primary forming method crucial for lightweight construction.

Based on this knowledge, students are able to determine the possibilities and limitations of joining manufacturing processes, compare, select, and characterize casting processes for selected components.
Students are able to propose suitable processes for the production of semi-finished or finished products with defined properties.
Students are able to carry out a targeted design of processes or tool systems through the imparted theoretical and practical knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to joining processes (process variants, advantages/disadvantages, application areas, application limits)
Thermal joining: Welding, Brazing, Laser beam welding
Mechanical joining: Semi-hollow punch riveting, Full punch riveting, Clinching, Blind riveting, . . .
Determination of properties of joined connections
assessment_rules: The module final examination (Klausur) will last 180-240 minutes. Students should explain the underlying elementary processes for exemplary problems, select suitable methods, and characterize them fundamentally. Credit points are awarded upon passing the module final examination.
